.h3 Description:
As a user, I want the ability to restore the visibility of the "Getting Started Resources" card within the OpenShift UI after having hidden it.

.h3 Acceptance Criteria:

This Jira story is raised in response to user feedback concerning the inability to regain visibility of the "Getting Started Resources" within the OpenShift UI after it has been hidden. The primary goal is to provide a user-friendly solution that enables users to easily restore the visibility of this pane, ensuring a seamless experience for navigating and accessing essential resources within the UI.

Goal : 
For first time users (who haven't set up their account association) we want to ensure they are aware of the Hands on Experience from the prerequisites page. 

Current UX:
On the prerequisites page the user is shown a lot of different actions they can take. They are not pushed to try the Hands on Experience. 

Ideal UX: 
The user will not be shown all of the prerequisites for setting up ROSA unless they choose to go down that path. They should be shown the option to Try ROSA first or begin their set up. 

Questions to explore:
Should we hide the page or just add an area at the top?
What happens if the user has tried the hands one experience one, twice, or has completed it?

items.fromString:
Problem:
Currently the user can go to the wizard (from a few different areas) without associating their account first. This results in an error and pushes them out of the wizard to first associate their account. 

Goal: 
Ensure users can only go to the wizard after they have associated their AWS account and/or tried the Hands on Experience.

Current UX:
In the create cluster page for ROSA there is the primary dropdown action to create a cluster (with CLI or Web interface) and a secondary action for prerequisites. 
Also, in the prerequisites page (at the bottom) you can go straight to the wizard.

Preferred UX (to be further explored by the designer):
In the create cluster ensure the user is pointed to Begin setup (prerequisites page) or TRY (Hands on Experience). Ensure the users current state is taken into account. 
1. If they have already tried the Hands on Experience we remove this option and point them to Begin Setup. 
2. If they associated an account we show the action to create cluster but also still show the Try secondary action.
3. If they have associated an account and have tried the Hands on Experience we show only the Create cluster dropdown action with options to create via wizard or show the CLI command to create. A secondary link can show the action to associate a new account.

In the prereqs page the action to go to the wizard should be removed unless they have associated their account. Also to be further explored by the designer.

items.fromString:
*[Figma design file|https://www.figma.com/file/kxPwMVM7ND02QgOCxlvghj/PID-limits---Day-2?type=design&node-id=0%3A1&mode=design&t=zaBiJUVjl8q9QQcE-1]*

_________________________________________
h3. *Feature Overview (aka. Goal Summary)*  

{color:#172b4d}This feature will introduce Process IDs (PIDs) as a node-level resource for application pods that customers can manage and control. {color}

{color:#172b4d}Process IDs and the number of processes are a fundamental resource on Linux hosts. Even when other resources like CPU, Storage, and Memory are available it is possible for some Pods to run out of process IDs and fail.{color}

{color:#172b4d}This feature will allow customers to increase/set PIDs per Pod as allowed by the node allocatable. The feature will be delivered across multiple milestones to cover for all use cases (cluster level, per-machinepool level) across different topologies (HCP, Classic).{color}
 # {color:#172b4d}M1 / XCMSTRAT-110 - API and ROSA CLI support on ROSA Classic{color}
 # {color:#172b4d}M2 / XCMSTRAT-355 - Support for ROSA HCP {color}
 # {color:#172b4d}M3/ XCMSTRAT-382 - Support for all clients (UI,TF), Per-Machinepool, all allowed Pidlimit values {color}
 # {color:#172b4d}Backlog/XCMSTRAT-383 - Support for day-1 (cluster installation){color}

{color:#172b4d}This Jira is pruned to include the first milestone: providing cluster-wide configuration on ROSA and OSD on AWS clusters. {color}

*Goals (aka. expected user outcomes)*
 * Configure podpidslimit for all worker nodes (i.e., all nodes of machine pools; all cluster nodes that are not control plane nodes)
 * PodPidsLimit values from 4096 (default) to 16,384 (soft limit) available to all clusters
 * No impacts to the control plane nodes.
 * When not set, the default value provided by OCP version will be applied. 
 * Support on OCP 4.11 and above
 * Customer can use ROSA CLI (MVP), OCM UI (follow-up) and Terraform (follow-up) to set this
 * Ability to modify this on an existing cluster - all nodes will be rebooted one at a time - potentially causing workload disruption
 * ROSA CLI and OCM UI to provide warning that changing this value will require machine pool nodes to reboot and disrupt the applications
 * Ability to set this configuration at the time of cluster creation (follow-up)
 * Support for ROSA clusters and OSD CCS on AWS clusters
 * ROSA and OSD DOCs updated how to use the feature.
 * OCM includes the field in the telemetry for tracking analytics on clusters that override the default values. 

h3. *Documentation*
 * The feature needs to be covered both creating and _editing_ machine pools section as requested in the OSDOCS-6267. i.e., cover in the day-2 workflows.
 * Provide an use case or reasoning to set this value from other than the default. 
 * Provide a section on considerations including:
 ** what happens if the value is not set
 ** what happens when the value is updated (rolling over to machines with reboot, disruptive to workloads)
 ** what happens when the value set gets exhausted (pods restarted/rescheduled?) etc.  

*Additional Information:*
 * *Opportunity:* With the standard default kubelet configuration that only allows a fixed 4K limit on PIDs per Pod, those workloads that need more PIDs per Pod are unable to run and operate on Managed Services. The prospects and customers who today do that in self-managed OCP are unable to adopt ROSA because of missing configurability.

{*}References{*}:
 # Kubelet configuration spec part of Machine API : [https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/rest_api/machine_apis/containerruntimeconfig-machineconfiguration-openshift-io-v1.html#spec-containerruntimeconfig]
 # Kubernetes documentation on per-pod PIDs [https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/pid-limiting/]

*[Figma design file|https://www.figma.com/file/kxPwMVM7ND02QgOCxlvghj/PID-limits---Day-2?type=design&node-id=0%3A1&mode=design&t=zaBiJUVjl8q9QQcE-1]*

 

_________________________________________
h3. *Feature Overview (aka. Goal Summary)*  

{color:#172b4d}This feature will introduce Process IDs (PIDs) as a node-level resource for application pods that customers can manage and control. {color}

{color:#172b4d}Process IDs and the number of processes are a fundamental resource on Linux hosts. Even when other resources like CPU, Storage, and Memory are available it is possible for some Pods to run out of process IDs and fail.{color}

{color:#172b4d}This feature will allow customers to increase/set PIDs per Pod as allowed by the node allocatable. The feature will be delivered across multiple milestones to cover for all use cases (cluster level, per-machinepool level) across different topologies (HCP, Classic).{color}
 # {color:#172b4d}M1 / XCMSTRAT-110 - API and ROSA CLI support on ROSA Classic{color}
 # {color:#172b4d}M2 / XCMSTRAT-355 - Support for ROSA HCP {color}
 # {color:#172b4d}M3/ XCMSTRAT-382 - Support for all clients (UI,TF), Per-Machinepool, all allowed Pidlimit values {color}
 # {color:#172b4d}Backlog/XCMSTRAT-383 - Support for day-1 (cluster installation){color}

{color:#172b4d}This Jira is pruned to include the first milestone: providing cluster-wide configuration on ROSA and OSD on AWS clusters. {color}

*Goals (aka. expected user outcomes)*
 * Configure podpidslimit for all worker nodes (i.e., all nodes of machine pools; all cluster nodes that are not control plane nodes)
 * PodPidsLimit values from 4096 (default) to 16,384 (soft limit) available to all clusters
 * No impacts to the control plane nodes.
 * When not set, the default value provided by OCP version will be applied. 
 * Support on OCP 4.11 and above
 * Customer can use ROSA CLI (MVP), OCM UI (follow-up) and Terraform (follow-up) to set this
 * Ability to modify this on an existing cluster - all nodes will be rebooted one at a time - potentially causing workload disruption
 * ROSA CLI and OCM UI to provide warning that changing this value will require machine pool nodes to reboot and disrupt the applications
 * Ability to set this configuration at the time of cluster creation (follow-up)
 * Support for ROSA clusters and OSD CCS on AWS clusters
 * ROSA and OSD DOCs updated how to use the feature.
 * OCM includes the field in the telemetry for tracking analytics on clusters that override the default values. 

h3. *Documentation*
 * The feature needs to be covered both creating and _editing_ machine pools section as requested in the OSDOCS-6267. i.e., cover in the day-2 workflows.
 * Provide an use case or reasoning to set this value from other than the default. 
 * Provide a section on considerations including:
 ** what happens if the value is not set
 ** what happens when the value is updated (rolling over to machines with reboot, disruptive to workloads)
 ** what happens when the value set gets exhausted (pods restarted/rescheduled?) etc.  

*Additional Information:*
 * *Opportunity:* With the standard default kubelet configuration that only allows a fixed 4K limit on PIDs per Pod, those workloads that need more PIDs per Pod are unable to run and operate on Managed Services. The prospects and customers who today do that in self-managed OCP are unable to adopt ROSA because of missing configurability.

{*}References{*}:
 # Kubelet configuration spec part of Machine API : [https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/rest_api/machine_apis/containerruntimeconfig-machineconfiguration-openshift-io-v1.html#spec-containerruntimeconfig]
 # Kubernetes documentation on per-pod PIDs [https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/pid-limiting/]

items.fromString:
Overview:

This feature will introduce transparency and visibility into cluster update end-to-end. OCM Console will provide a dedicated TAB for configuring, monitoring and tracking progress of cluster update.

Current Gaps:
 # Managed OpenShift's advantage is cluster update orchestrated and monitored by RH SRE. Yet, under the Cluster, the OCM Console does not have a dedicated section for Cluster update. The Cluster update configuration is under wrongly-named 'Settings' tab.
 # When the upgrade is requested, there's a lag for few minutes before the scheduled upgrade is displayed in the screen. The user expectation is that the UI show the configured/requested cluster update immediately - perhaps with a status pending which changes to scheduled upon API response return. 
 # After the cluster update is scheduled, there is no granular tracking across milestones. Service Logs come informing terminal statuses or delays but there's no way to track where in the update process the requested upgrade is.

Overview:

This feature will introduce transparency and visibility into cluster update end-to-end. (Read more in the parent XCMSTRAT).

Current Gaps:
 # Managed OpenShift's advantage is cluster update orchestrated and monitored by RH SRE. Yet, under the Cluster, the OCM Console does not have a dedicated section for Cluster update. The Cluster update configuration is under oddly-named 'Settings' tab.
 # When the upgrade is requested, there's a lag for few minutes before the scheduled upgrade is displayed in the screen (refer to HAC-5092 linked). The user expectation is that the UI show the configured/requested cluster update immediately - perhaps with a status pending which changes to scheduled upon API response return. 
 # After the cluster update is scheduled, there is no granular tracking across milestones. Service Logs come informing terminal statuses or delays but there's no way to track where in the update process the requested upgrade is. 

Proposal:
 # A dedicated TAB with title Updates/Upgrades containing following 3 sub-sections:
 ** Update Configuration : existing functionalities such as one-time or recurring update, node-drain, and target version
 ** Update Monitoring: New progress bar that shows high level milestones of upgrades end to end.
 ** Update History/Analytics: New section to provide KPIs and analytics around past cluster updates: From/to OCP version, Duration of updates, Active Node(s), Drain Period.

items.fromString:
*Background* *Info*

Today a user that visits the OpenShift (OCM) bundle is initially landed on the Cluster list. If no clusters exist, the user is prompted to create a cluster. The user can also switch to the Overview page and some amount of information will be shown about available services that can run on OpenShift, though this page hasn't been updated in some time.

There is a need for a landing place inside of the OpenShift bundle that orients a (new) user to what OpenShift can do for them and what OpenShift offerings there are, as well as likely what services they can use with OpenShift. Consideration should be given to how this page fits into an existing user's experience too, would they want to see this information or just info about their clusters. 

*Goals*
 * Determine what information about OpenShift and it's offerings should be reflected to users (new and existing)
 ** Determine what CTAs are needed for each OpenShift offering, and if there is need for additional product-specific pages in console (additional UX story)
 * Determine how related services can be cross-sold to users
 * Confirm this page is not a hinderance to existing users that might be mostly interested in viewing info about their clusters
 * Make sure this page fits into the overall working group around console landing pages, led by [~accountid:557058:78b37446-6818-4ae8-8fb9-02b4cfbecdc7] and [~accountid:5b0ea3e8e249415c02f67c16]
 * Users may be brought into console from a ROSA marketing site, and specifically land on a ROSA-specific page like the "get started" page. Confirm if they navigate back to a top level console page that they can be find the ROSA-related content, likely via this new overview page. Also, could search play a role here?
 ** How would the left nav be affected by this new pages presence? 

{*}D{*}{*}efinition of Done{*} - targeted for 236
 * Create design deliverable capturing Goal deliverables
 * Link design in this story
 * Review with all relevant stakeholders including [~accountid:61f179dee218f0006af2886d] [~accountid:70121:0147f97a-c89b-4007-85f0-8b7e35412661]

*Designs & Other Artifacts*

As a user of the Hybrid Cloud Console, I want a dedicated Learning Resources page within the OpenShift Cluster Manager (OCM) section of the console. This page should provide a centralized collection of helpful resources, both internal and external, to aid in understanding and utilizing OCM effectively. This will enhance the user experience by eliminating the need to navigate to separate sites for documentation, thereby saving time and effort.{*}{{*}}

 
h1. Acceptance Criteria:
 * The page should contain categorized links to relevant in-product documentation, guides, tutorials, and other helpful resources related to OCM.
 * External resources, such as cloud.redhat.com and developer.redhat.com, should be mapped out and linked from this page.
 * The categories on the Learning Resources page should be logically organized, such as "Getting Started," "Tutorials," "Best Practices," and "Advanced Topics."
 * Each resource link should have a concise title and a brief description to provide context.
 * Analytics tracking should be integrated to monitor user engagement and improve the quality of the resources over time.
 * The development of the Learning Resources page should follow the established design and development standards of the Hybrid Cloud Console.

h1. Definition of done:
 * Identified and published relevant materials to the learning resources page
 * Work with Cloud dot and RHD to ensure cross-linking across our sites.

This is a placeholder ticket for providing admins the flexibility to provision the OSD clusters on GCP with and without UEFISecureBoot (i.e. with or without "constraints/compute.requireShieldedVm" policy). 

For more details on the feature, refer XCMSTRAT-115

 

Update, July 17, 2023 (post discussion with SREPs)
 - Enabling Secure Boot by default can impact the ability to load GPU drivers if they are unsigned. Ref: [https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus/install-drivers-gpu#secure-boot]] 
 - Therefore, it was decided to have admin users explicitly opt in for "platform.gcp.defaultMachinePlatform.secureBoot" when provisioning the OSD cluster on GCP. This is assumed to be enabled/disabled by a new field in the OCM UI.
 - Based on whether "platform.gcp.defaultMachinePlatform.secureBoot" is enabled or disabled, the admin must ensure "constraints/compute.requireShieldedVm" policy is in or NOT in place in the GCP console. 
Background: Before implementing this feature, the admin must ensure "constraints/compute.requireShieldedVm" policy is NOT place as listed in the [OSD documentation|https://docs.openshift.com/dedicated/osd_planning/gcp-ccs.html#ccs-gcp-customer-procedure_gcp-ccs].

h1. Customer Problem

The current signup process for the Red Hat Developer Sandbox is on the Red Hat Developers webpage, which can be confusing and inconvenient for users primarily working within the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console. To improve the user experience and streamline the onboarding process, there is a need to move the signup process for the Developer Sandbox to the Hybrid Cloud Console.
h1. Business Case

By moving the signup process for the Red Hat Developer Sandbox to the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console, we can achieve the following benefits:
h3. Improved User Experience

Simplifying and streamlining the signup process will result in a more seamless user onboarding experience.
h3. Increased Adoption

Making the signup process more accessible and convenient can lead to more users adopting the Developer Sandbox.
h3. Enhanced Brand Image

Showcasing a user-friendly and efficient process will improve our brand image and reinforce our commitment to customer satisfaction.
h3. Cross-Product Synergy

We can promote awareness and usage of other Red Hat products and services by integrating the signup process into the Hybrid Cloud Console.
h1. User Stories
 * As a developer, I want to quickly sign up for the Red Hat Developer Sandbox from the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console to streamline my onboarding experience.

h1.  
 * As an IT manager, I want my team to have a seamless and convenient signup process for the Red Hat Developer Sandbox, ensuring they can quickly access and utilize the available resources.

h1.  
 * As a system administrator, I want to manage my team's access to the Red Hat Developer Sandbox and other Red Hat products within the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console, simplifying the overall management process.

h1. Product Needs
h2. Integrate Signup Process into Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console
 * Develop a seamless and user-friendly Red Hat Developer Sandbox signup process within the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console.
 * Ensure the signup process includes all necessary steps, such as accepting terms and conditions, providing user details, and setting up authentication.

h2. Single Sign-On (SSO) Support
 * Implement Single Sign-On (SSO) support to allow users to access the Red Hat Developer Sandbox and other Red Hat products with a single set of credentials.

h2. Documentation and Tutorials

items.fromString:
The requirements as taken from: https://issues.redhat.com/browse/HAC-3752:

 
This feature will allow customers to select their own sizing (within our provided constraints such as minimums, maximums) for the disk volumes of their worker machinepool nodes for ROSA HCP.

Customers will need the option to select the sizing for the default machinepool at cluster install-time.

Customers will need the option to select the sizing for the new day2 machinepools (after the cluster is installed).

This feature will not allow the resizing of existing machinepool node volumes.

 

Design doc from ROSA Classic: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jgHGMqEXiJJVdkF1riM7YxG4oJR4Zv-1-4bHDc4jeEE/edit?usp=sharing]

*Background* *Info*

https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCM-139 brings in the support for the setting IMDSv2.

The requirements on how to expose this in the UI are:
 * There is a need to expose a new configuration value which can have one of two values:
 ** "use both IMDSv1 and IMDSv2" (default) 
 ** "use IMDSv2 only"
 * Technically it is a machine pool scoped setting which can be changed per machine pool. But the requirement is to set this only once per cluster. All the machine pools will be using this one setting
 * This is a day1 only setting. Once the cluster is installed, this can not be changed. Also all the machine pools added in day2 will use the setting configured on cluster creation
 * There are no restrictions on when is this allowed (e.g. it works with all OCP versions)

For details, see a slack thread: [https://redhat-internal.slack.com/archives/C0534HDGBNW/p1683033244824409]

*Goals*
 * Create updated design for ROSA wizard (and other wizards?) that includes a new setting for machine pools to use IMDS v1 or v2
 * Determine if this setting needs to be reflected in day 2 cluster settings
